hero.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting on Southeast Rivergreen Circle in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots. When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries.

Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Judlin Stokes, 22. Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved.

Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police. The department emphasized that they do not believe the broader community faces any danger related to this incident.

The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters following hazing investigation
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024. The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally.

Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others. The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process.

cards.headline: Lightning strikes cause brush fire and house fire in Port St. Lucie during severe weather
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to a brush fire and house fire in Port St. Lucie as severe weather brought heavy lightning activity to the area Friday.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. At the time of the storm, radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area. St. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Video sent to the newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. Moore O'Rourke said all of a sudden, it got black, the wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like she had not seen. Severe weather stretched all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning.

cards.headline: Five cyclospora cases confirmed on Treasure Coast since May as residents avoid lettuce
cards.teaser: Two confirmed cases in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County are among five local cyclospora infections reported since May, according to the Florida Department of Health.
cards.body:
Two confirmed cases in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County are among five local cyclospora infections reported since May, according to the Florida Department of Health. Two additional cases were confirmed in Palm Beach County. The outbreaks are tied to contaminated produce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like melon, bananas and avocados. She recommends washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein.

Barone's biggest warning is to avoid bagged lettuce if possible. She recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. She recommends cleaning produce using a 1-to-3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water.

cards.teaser: The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St. Lucie Mets 7-4 on Saturday night, evening their series and setting up a decisive finale Sunday. The Cardinals built an early lead and held off a late rally by the Mets.

The loss comes one day after the Mets won 3-2 in extra innings on Friday night. St. Lucie pushed back late in Saturday's contest but could not overcome Palm Beach's advantage.

The series between the two Florida State League teams will be decided in Sunday's game. Both clubs are fighting for playoff positioning as the season continues.

The finale represents a critical game for the Mets, who will look to bounce back from Saturday's defeat and take the series at home.

cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened the three-game series at one game apiece and set up a rubber match Sunday afternoon.

Palm Beach opened the scoring with three runs in the bottom of the first inning. Brayden Smith singled to center field, and an error by D'Andre Smith allowed the Cardinals to capitalize. Ryan Weingartner and Sebastian Dos Santos scored on the play before Brayden Smith came around to give Palm Beach a 3-0 advantage.

St. Lucie responded with two runs in the second inning.

Chase Meggers delivered an RBI single with runners on the corners, scoring AJ Salgado. Jeremy Rodriguez then brought Simon Juan home on a fielder's choice to cut the Cardinals' lead to 3-2.

Palm Beach began pulling away in the fourth inning. Alex Birg drove in Yordalin Pena with an RBI single before Dos Santos launched a two-run home run. The Cardinals eventually built a 7-2 lead.

The Mets bullpen settled the game down after Joe Scarborough entered from the bullpen. Scarborough delivered two scoreless and hitless innings while striking out four batters.

It marked Scarborough's second consecutive scoreless appearance at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Antonio Jimenez gave the Mets another run in the top of the sixth inning with a solo home run. It was Jimenez's sixth homer of the season and his fourth during July, cutting the Palm Beach lead to 7-3.

Caden Wooster followed Scarborough with another strong relief appearance. Wooster allowed just one hit over two scoreless innings and struck out four.

Scarborough and Wooster combined to strike out eight batters over four shutout innings. St. Lucie's pitching staff finished the game with 12 strikeouts, reaching double digits for the second consecutive night.

The Mets mounted one final rally in the ninth inning and brought the potential tying run to the plate. Palm Beach reliever Nathan Shinn escaped the threat and secured the victory for the Cardinals.

St. Lucie fell to 7-14 in the second half and 40-47 overall. Palm Beach improved to 13-9 in the second half and 65-42 overall.

The teams will decide the series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 12:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County with residential pools.

According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program offers one alarm per household to Martin County residents who have a residential pool. There are no income or priority group requirements for the program.

The alarms are available while supplies last. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. Dambeck said it's just the way that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. Ahern said if they hung in there, it would have worked and would have built up pretty good, noting the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is easy and close. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said Boston is seeing great demand. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Dambeck said the door is not closed for the JFK route to return, noting they'll evaluate continuously and just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back.

hero.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record with 3:42.66
hero.teaser: Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999.
hero.body:
A 27-year-old world record fell Saturday in London when Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. Kerr made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. The shoe company said Friday that this was the moment Kerr stood to make history and bring the mile record home.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final Sunday with President Trump attending
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement and private companies have prepared for two years to secure Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey, where President Trump will attend the trophy presentation.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be addressed from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi bathed Lamine Yamal as baby, now face off in World Cup final
cards.teaser: Photos from 2007 show a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a charity calendar shoot. The two soccer stars will face each other Sunday when Argentina plays Spain in the World Cup final.
cards.body:
Almost two decades ago, photographer Joan Monfort didn't think much of his photo shoot of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a cute baby boy in a plastic bathtub. Not until the remarkable twist of fate became clear years later, when that infant blossomed into Lamine Yamal. Now those images of the longhaired Messi, his hands covered in soap suds, have become the most talked about in the runup to Sunday's World Cup final, when Messi's Argentina will play Yamal's Spain for the biggest trophy in the sport. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the AP, took the photos in 2007 as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Luck dictated that Yamal's mother, who appears in the calendar photo, won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate.

Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but now with the World Cup final looming, Monfort said interest in his photos has skyrocketed. The 58-year-old photographer said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets, while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. Monfort told the AP from his home in Barcelona that the coincidence has tested his skepticism. "I have never been a believer or thought that anything was destined to occur, but I am beginning to have my doubts. This is beyond all reasonable explanations," he said.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program, led by Summer Faerman, connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts. The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012.

The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds, David Jolly Lead Florida Governor's Race as Primary Nears
hero.teaser: Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey rele
hero.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republicans, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8%, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and received President Donald Trump's endorsement.

Collins, who was appointed lieutenant governor by Gov. Ron DeSantis in August 2025, has not received DeSantis's endorsement. During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, saying the primary is between Donalds and himself. Meanwhile, Fishback faces pressure on two fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments.

Collins is also challenging whether Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing on the residency question is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. The residency challenge adds another complication to Fishback's campaign as he attempts to gain traction in a race where Donalds maintains a significant polling advantage over the rest of the Republican field.

On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities, with the alleged scheme operating from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, and Govoni served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. The connection nonetheless presents a challenge for Jolly as he seeks to maintain his lead in the Democratic primary while managing questions about his past associations with individuals now facing serious federal charges.

hero.headline: Halloween flight from Stuart airport to Georgia documented
hero.teaser: A family flight in a Piper Aztec departed Stuart airport bound for Baxley, Georgia on a Halloween trip.
hero.body:
A Piper Aztec aircraft flew from Stuart airport to Baxley, Georgia carrying a family on a Halloween flight. The flight departed from KSUA, the identifier for Witham Field in Stuart, and landed at KBHC in Baxley.

The flight represents general aviation activity at Stuart's Witham Field airport. Witham Field serves private pilots and small aircraft in Martin County.

The Piper Aztec is a twin-engine aircraft commonly used for personal and family flights. The flight was documented as part of a Halloween family trip from the Treasure Coast to Georgia.

cards.teaser: The annual Fort Pierce event connects families with services and public safety demonstrations.
cards.body:
Unity in the Community took place in Fort Pierce, bringing together families with community services and public safety demonstrations. The annual event provides resources to Fort Pierce residents.

The event connects families with local services and allows residents to interact with public safety officials through demonstrations and community outreach activities.

hero.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian as severe weather strikes Treasure Coast
hero.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom captured the waterspout moving through the area.

The severe weather stretched across the region, bringing heavy rain and significant lightning activity. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters recorded video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said.

Lightning strikes caused fires in Port St. Lucie. Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening. Radar picked up significant lightning in the area at the time, though Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

The severe weather extended to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Moore O'Rourke summarized what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather reminded residents of nature's unpredictable power.
